scope: Pre-refinement assessment of epic clarity and boundaries. This does not replace discovery, prioritization, or team estimation.

scoring.note: Criteria with implemented=false carry no points and do not affect score or ready gate.

assessmentRules.readyGate: An epic cannot be 'Ready' if any required criterion is 'flag' or 'not-assessable'.
assessmentRules.assessmentIncomplete: If Ollama is unavailable or model checks fail, assessment status is 'incomplete' and must be retried.

criteria.passCondition: A goal section or phrase exists and at least two of three SMART hints (specific, measurable, time-bound) are detected.
A benefit section or phrase exists and contains a quantification (number with unit, or reduce/increase/save).

criteria.description: Lists child stories by issue number.
criteria.passCondition: At least one issue reference (#n) is present in the body.

criteria.description: Flags signs that the epic is too large.
criteria.passCondition: Estimated size is S or M; L and XL fail.
indicators: Programme-level scope across several product domains or platforms
Several independent customer outcomes in one epic
Words such as 'all', 'every', or 'complete' without a narrow boundary
No coherent product boundary that a single team could own

criteria.passCondition: The goal identifies a user or business outcome and is not merely a technology or activity label.
The model can quote the intended benefit without inventing one.

criteria.description: Names at least product and target group; operator and platforms are recommended.
criteria.passCondition: Product and target group are stated in structured context or clearly stated prose.

criteria.description: Has an explicit in-scope and out-of-scope boundary.
criteria.passCondition: Both sections are present and contain at least one meaningful item.

criteria.description: Provides a measurable outcome or explicitly flags that a baseline/target still needs product validation.
criteria.passCondition: A measure is stated without fabricated certainty, or the missing measurement is transparently flagged.

criteria.description: Can be broken into independently discussable candidate stories or thin vertical slices.
criteria.passCondition: The model proposes or validates at least two distinct user-value slices, with evidence from the epic.

criteria.description: Names one accountable owner for the epic.
criteria.passCondition: An owner is explicitly named with a role or team.

criteria.description: Names the relevant stakeholder groups or people.
criteria.passCondition: At least one stakeholder group is explicitly named; impacted or approving stakeholders should be identifiable.

criteria.description: Links the epic to an overarching company or product goal.
criteria.passCondition: The company or product objective is explicitly stated or linked. The model must not invent the relationship.

criteria.description: Defines meaningful milestones for the epic.
criteria.passCondition: At least two milestones are stated, or the epic explicitly flags milestones as an open planning question.
A start, target, timeframe, or explicitly open timeline question is present.
Known risks have mitigations, or the epic transparently flags risk discovery as open.
Dependencies are named with affected team/system, or the epic explicitly states that dependency discovery is open.

criteria.description: Existing child stories have traceable GitHub links and current statuses.
criteria.passCondition: Referenced child issues exist in GitHub, point back to the epic, and their status is reported; missing links are flagged.

examples.title: Invoice self-service
examples.summary: Outcome, benefit, scope boundaries, candidate stories, owner, stakeholders, milestones, and a deliberately cautious success-measure statement are present.

examples.title: Modernize the portal
examples.body: The customer portal should be modern and better.

examples.title: Digital customer experience
examples.body: Build web and mobile experiences for onboarding, billing, payments, support, notifications, profile management, and all account changes for every customer segment.
examples.expectedObservation: Programme-level scope across multiple domains and platforms; recommend split by customer outcome or product domain.
